questions.question: Differentiate between direct and indirect printing.
questions.solution_html:
• In direct printing the image is transferred directly from the printing plate or image carrier to the paper.
  • e.g., Letterpress printing and gravure printing. In indirect printing the image i s transferred first to an
  • intermediate surface and then to the paper . e.g., Offset printing.

questions.question: What is the difference between make-up and layout?
questions.solution_html:
• Layout is the preliminary plan of a printing job. It is the plan for arranging elements on a page,
  • whereas make-up is the process of assembling those elements into complete pages ready for printing.
  • It assembles text, illustrations and other elements into the required page format.

  • before publication. Editing involves improving a manuscript before publication.

questions.question: Explain the different types of paper used in publishing.
questions.solution_html:
• A publisher select s paper based on quality, weight, surface, durability, printing requirements, and
  • production cost. The two important paper sizes are International DIN system and Standard English
  • paper sizes. In DIN system paper sizes are A series, B series and C series. A series is the only one
  • used for book work. The commonly used Standard English paper sizes are Crown, Demy, Foolscap,
  • Royal, Medium, Large Post, Imperial etc.
